subsystems.name: Electrode threads
subsystems.role: record electrical spikes from individual neurons and, in some designs, stimulate them.

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplify, digitise and process neural signals inside the skull.
parts: inductive coil for power and data

subsystems.name: Surgical insertion robot
subsystems.role: places each flexible thread at a precise depth while avoiding blood vessels.
parts: needle to carry and release the thread
optical imaging to map surface vasculature

subsystems.name: External decoder and user interface
subsystems.role: translates recorded neural activity into control commands for a computer, cursor or prosthetic.

subsystems.name: Wireless power and data link
subsystems.role: charges the implant and streams high-bandwidth neural data through intact skin.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate electrode threads
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography patterns metal electrodes and traces on a thin polymer film, which is then cut into dozens of flexible threads, each carrying many recording sites.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the implant
buildSteps.detail: The threads are electrically bonded to a custom chip that amplifies and digitises their signals; the chip and coil are sealed into a hermetic case.

buildSteps.title: Build the surgical robot
buildSteps.detail: A precision robot is assembled with a needle mechanism and imaging system that can insert each thread to a planned depth without hitting surface blood vessels.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and package
buildSteps.detail: The implant and surgical tools are cleaned in a cleanroom and sterilised for human use.

buildSteps.title: Implant the device
buildSteps.detail: A surgeon removes a small piece of skull, the robot inserts the threads into the cortex, and the implant is seated flush with the skull and closed over.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and train
buildSteps.detail: Neural activity is recorded while the user attempts specific actions; software learns to map those patterns to cursor or prosthetic movements.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and update
buildSteps.detail: The implant is charged wirelessly and its firmware can be updated remotely; long-term performance depends on electrode stability and tissue response.

prerequisites.why: rigid arrays like the Utah Array have been used in humans for decades, but flexible polymer threads that survive years in the brain are still being proven.
sealing electronics against body fluid for a decade is difficult; the implant must not leak or corrode.
streaming thousands of neural channels through skin without wires requires low-power chips and reliable inductive links.
translating spike patterns into intended movement or speech is improving but still needs frequent recalibration.
the brain's immune response can gradually insulate electrodes, reducing signal quality over years.

pathway.milestone: early human trials of intracortical implants for paralysis, e.g. Neuralink's first human implant in 2024 and ongoing academic trials
pathway.unlocks: proof that people can control external devices with thought in daily life.

pathway.milestone: larger clinical trials for communication, cursor control and robotic arm use
pathway.unlocks: data on safety, reliability and how long implants last.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval for limited medical use in severe paralysis
pathway.unlocks: routine clinical availability for a narrow group of patients.

pathway.milestone: higher-channel, bidirectional implants and exploration of other conditions such as depression or epilepsy
pathway.unlocks: broader medical applications, though mental-health uses remain speculative.
